mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's RECENT_5 shots FOR exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR by a meaningful margin, AND Team B's RECENT_5 shots AGAINST is also elevated above its ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST. Measure whether goals per shot in such joint-elevated-volume matchups differs from the baseline conversion rate implied by each team's individual shot and goal averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both attacking volume (Team A shots FOR RECENT_5 elevated) and defensive exposure (Team B shots AGAINST RECENT_5 elevated) are simultaneously high, goals per shot may saturate or be suppressed relative to the product of individual averages — i.e., volume and conversion do not scale linearly together.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent surge in shots and shots-on-target (RECENT_5) relative to its long-run average co-occurs with a simultaneous compression in Team B's recent shots allowed (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR). The joint condition — one team's attack volume rising while the opponent's defensive solidity is also rising — may suppress the conversion rate (goals per shot) relative to what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR for Team A and shots AGAINST for Team B) simultaneously, and examining a derived ratio (goals per shot) rather than either observable in isolation. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's shots_on_target FOR RECENT_5 is elevated above ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST RECENT_5 is elevated above ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint condition, test whether corner_kicks FOR (Team A) and AGAINST (Team B) are elevated relative to competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent on-target shot profiles are elevated simultaneously, corner kick volume rises above competition context baseline — reflecting sustained attacking pressure that does not convert cleanly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR, while Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST has also risen in RECENT_5. The asymmetric relationship between one team's on-target accuracy trend and the opponent's recent defensive on-target concession trend — measured jointly — may predict whether corner kicks (a proxy for sustained attacking pressure without conversion) are elevated above competition norms.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots_on_target FOR for Team A and shots_on_target AGAINST for Team B) and relating their joint state to a third observable (corner_kicks). Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's offsides FOR RECENT_5 being elevated above ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's offsides AGAINST RECENT_5 being elevated above ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint condition, compare the ratio of first-half goals to second-half goals for both teams against their unconditional first-half/second-half goal splits.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent offside profiles are jointly elevated, the share of goals scored in the first half rises relative to the unconditional first-half/second-half goal split — reflecting high-line pressing dynamics that produce earlier scoring opportunities.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR (and relative to its home vs away split), while Team B's offsides AGAINST has also risen in RECENT_5. The joint condition of both teams' offside profiles shifting simultaneously — one team pressing higher lines, the other conceding more offsides — may be associated with a distinct pattern in first-half versus second-half goal distribution, as high-line pressing tends to produce early goals but also fatigue-related second-half exposure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides FOR for Team A and offsides AGAINST for Team B) and relating their joint state to a within-match temporal split (first-half vs second-half goals). This combines a two-observable joint condition with a half-level resolution, neither of which is covered individually.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team B's corner kicks FOR showing a large home-vs-away gap (home ALL_PRIOR >> away ALL_PRIOR), AND (b) Team B's RECENT_5 corners FOR being below their away ALL_PRIOR. Test whether the combined match corner total is suppressed relative to the naive sum of Team A FOR ALL_PRIOR and Team B FOR ALL_PRIOR averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's corner production is both venue-asymmetric (much higher at home) and in a recent downward regime, the combined match corner total is suppressed below the naive sum of both teams' unconditional averages — the venue asymmetry and recent regime interact non-additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kicks FOR show a pronounced home/away asymmetry (home ALL_PRIOR substantially higher than away ALL_PRIOR), while their RECENT_5 corners FOR has dropped sharply below both their ALL_PRIOR and their away average. Simultaneously, Team A's corner kicks FOR is stable across home/away. The joint condition — one team's corner production being venue-asymmetric AND in a recent downward regime — may predict whether the combined corner total in this match is suppressed relative to the sum of each team's individual ALL_PRIOR averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct dimensions for Team B (venue asymmetry as a ratio of home vs away averages, AND recent-vs-long-run regime shift), and relating their joint state to the combined total. A single observable with one coarse band cannot capture this two-dimensional conditioning.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's possession FOR RECENT_5 being elevated above its ALL_PRIOR AND above its home ALL_PRIOR baseline, AND (b) Team B's possession FOR RECENT_5 being below its ALL_PRIOR. Within this joint diverging-possession condition, test whether Team B's fouls FOR and cards_2h FOR are elevated relative to their unconditional averages and competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When possession trends diverge asymmetrically — one team rising, the other falling in RECENT_5 — the possession-losing team's foul rate and second-half card rate rise above their unconditional averages, with the relationship being stronger than what either team's possession level alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession FOR has risen sharply in RECENT_5 relative to ALL_PRIOR (and relative to its home average), while Team B's possession FOR has dropped in RECENT_5 below its ALL_PRIOR. This creates an asymmetric possession regime shift where one team is trending toward dominance and the other toward submission. The joint condition of diverging possession trends — rather than either team's possession level alone — may be associated with elevated fouls AGAINST for the possession-losing team (Team B committing more fouls as they chase the ball), and consequently elevated cards_2h for Team B in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession FOR for Team A trending up AND possession FOR for Team B trending down) and relating their joint divergence to a third observable (fouls/cards) for the possession-losing side. This is an asymmetric cross-team two-observable joint condition, not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.
